problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual budget across 19 different infrastructure projects to maximize overall community benefit.  
The characteristics of each project are as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.055, disruption index 0.085, allocation limits [0.086, 0.356]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.136, disruption index 0.170, allocation limits [0.028, 0.597]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.169, disruption index 0.285, allocation limits [0.051, 0.517]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.164, disruption index 0.069, allocation limits [0.023, 0.803]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.124, disruption index 0.037, allocation limits [0.075, 0.534]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.043, disruption index 0.137, allocation limits [0.075, 0.595]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.135, disruption index 0.192, allocation limits [0.074, 0.313]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.196, disruption index 0.182, allocation limits [0.063, 0.344]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.051, disruption index 0.018, allocation limits [0.026, 0.876]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.183, disruption index 0.215, allocation limits [0.089, 0.346]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.113, disruption index 0.277, allocation limits [0.060, 0.712]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.099, disruption index 0.033, allocation limits [0.061, 0.525]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.038, disruption index 0.121, allocation limits [0.055, 0.488]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.164, disruption index 0.225, allocation limits [0.010, 0.845]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.111, disruption index 0.048, allocation limits [0.044, 0.785]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.134, disruption index 0.142, allocation limits [0.057, 0.408]  
* Project Q: benefit score 0.161, disruption index 0.193, allocation limits [0.010, 0.306]  
* Project R: benefit score 0.172, disruption index 0.114, allocation limits [0.027, 0.407]  
* Project S: benefit score 0.133, disruption index 0.080, allocation limits [0.085, 0.640]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified allocation limits, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to 1. To address immediate public needs, the planner requires that the subset of quick-impact projects, Q = {D, K}, collectively receive at least 0.083 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall disruption index for the portfolio must not exceed 0.178, and the total benefit score must be at least 0.092. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
